bmw.intro: Runsten reads your BMW or MINI through BMW CarData, the official service BMW opens to owners, free of charge: the car pushes its readings (battery, range, charging, odometer, position) and Runsten receives them. You create your own client ID in the MyBMW or MyMINI portal; Runsten never asks for your BMW password, and never sends a command to the car.

refused.body: BMW refused Runsten's connection on {time}: it was left unused for two weeks, or the client ID's subscription was withdrawn in the portal. Your cars are not read until you connect again; what was read stays.

delete.title: Remove your BMW connection?
delete.text: Your BMW and MINI cars stay, with their history, but are no longer read until you connect again. Runsten erases its tokens; the client ID stays in the portal, where you can delete it.

steps.title: Create your client ID in BMW's portal
steps.create: On a computer, sign in to the MyBMW or MyMINI portal, open the “BMW CarData” tile and choose “Create CarData Client”.
steps.subscribe: Subscribe the client to both CarData API and CarData Streaming, one at a time: wait for the first to be confirmed before the second.
steps.stream: Then configure the stream: tick the data keys the guide lists, so that the car pushes them.
steps.note: Note the client ID right away, then paste it below. Never click “Authenticate device” in the portal: Runsten does it.
